info.name: WaveFunctionFX
info.comment: Generates decorative wave-function plots as colour images or scalar fields.

description.p: The WaveFunctionFX class is a source effect that plots the magnitude of a hydrogen-like atomic orbital. It takes no input, and the result is intended for decorative patterns and textures rather than scientific visualisation.

The quantum numbers N, L and M select the shape of the orbital, and Scale sets its size. Drawing clamps them to N >= 1, 0 <= L < N and 0 <= M <= L, and the clamped values are written back to the object. If the clamped N + L exceeds 170, the formula cannot be evaluated in double precision and the field is zero. Samples that cannot be computed as finite values are also zero.

The plot is generated in a square domain of Resolution pixels and fitted to the primitive subregion according to AspectRatio and ResampleMethod. CentreX and CentreY position the centre of the orbital within the domain. The generated samples are retained until a field that changes them is modified, so a fixed Resolution avoids regenerating the plot when only the size of the target changes.

By default the magnitude is scaled so that the largest sample is one; see Normalisation. In IMAGE mode the samples are drawn in greyscale, or through the colour ramp defined by ColourMap or Stops. Set OutputMode to HEIGHT to produce a floating-point scalar field for numerical inputs, such as the height map of an enhanced LightingFX or the amount mask of a CompositeFX.
SVG documents can use the effect with the xvg:feWaveFunction element.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

description.p: Note that drawing the wave function will result in the N, L and M parameters being clamped to their valid ranges and this will be reflected in the object once the method returns.

field.name: CentreX
field.comment: Positions the plot centre from the left of the generation domain.

description.p: The value is a finite fraction in [0, 1] and defaults to 0.5.

field.name: CentreY
field.comment: Positions the plot centre from the top of the generation domain.

description.p: The value is a finite fraction in [0, 1] and defaults to 0.5.

field.name: ColourMap
field.comment: Assigns a pre-defined colourmap to the wave function.

description.p: An alternative to defining colour Stops in a wave function is available in the form of named colourmaps. Declaring a colourmap in this field will automatically populate the wave function's gradient with the colours defined in the map.

We currently support the following established colourmaps from the matplotlib and seaborn projects: cmap:crest, cmap:flare, cmap:icefire, cmap:inferno, cmap:magma, cmap:mako, cmap:plasma, cmap:rocket, cmap:viridis.
Setting a colourmap replaces custom stops. Set an empty string to clear the active ramp and draw in greyscale.
Writes accept non-negative integers. Drawing clamps the value to the range 0 <= L < N.
Writes accept any integer. Drawing clamps the value to the range 0 <= M <= L.
Writes accept positive integers. For the range of the wave formula, see WaveFunctionFX.

field.name: Normalisation
field.comment: Controls scaling of the generated magnitude before resampling.

field.name: OutputMode
field.comment: Selects a colour image or a floating-point scalar surface.

description.p: IMAGE is the default. HEIGHT emits unquantised samples and ignores the active colour ramp. NATIVE is unsupported.

field.name: ResampleMethod
field.comment: Selects the interpolation used when fitting the plot to the primitive.

field.name: Resolution
field.comment: The pixel resolution of the internally rendered wave function.

description.p: Values from 2 to 65535 fix the generation resolution. Odd values round down to an even number for drawing. Values 0 (the default) and 1 use the smaller filter-region dimension, rounded down to an even number. Fixed resolution allows reuse of the generated samples when the target size changes. The render must fit the filter surface budget.

field.name: Scale
field.comment: A finite positive multiplier that affects the scale of the plot.

field.name: Stops
field.comment: Defines the colours to use for the wave function.

description.p: The colours that will be used for drawing a wave function can be defined by the Stops array. At least two stops are required to define a start and end point for interpolating the gradient colours.
Setting stops replaces any named colourmap. Set an empty array to clear the active ramp and draw in greyscale.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Describes the primitive using the FilterEffect.XMLDef format.

constants.comment: Output modes for ImageFX, TurbulenceFX, BlurFX and WaveFunctionFX.
constants.const: Produce a linear floating-point scalar surface for numerical filter inputs.
Produce the usual RGBA image. This is the default.
BlurFX preserves its input format, including scalar and vector floats.
Selects a resampling method automatically. The choice depends on the operation.
Uses a broad Bessel filter that can preserve detail during resampling, but is slower than the smaller-kernel methods.
Produces a similar result to BILINEAR at a slightly higher CPU cost and a marginally sharper after-effect.
Bilinear is a common algorithm that produces a reasonable quality image quickly.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result will be less sharp than SINC.
Uses a Gaussian filter that softens the result, reducing aliasing at the cost of sharp edge detail.
Uses a Kaiser-windowed filter, giving smooth interpolation with low ringing and a cost close to BILINEAR.
This well known algorithm may serve as a point of comparison for evaluating the results of other methods. It shares characteristics with SINC and BLACKMAN.
Uses a Mitchell-Netravali filter, balancing sharpness and smoothness at a cost similar to BICUBIC.
Nearest neighbour is the fastest sampler at the cost of poor quality.
Uses a quadratic filter with a modest kernel, giving smoother results than BILINEAR with limited extra cost.
Five times slower than BILINEAR, the final result is of very good quality.

About twice as slow as BILINEAR, this method samples a 4x4 area and produces a considerably better result, and is a good choice for enlarging images without producing artifacts when contrasting colours are present.
Scales the largest generated sample to one. This is the default.
Preserve the magnitude of the generated samples.
